thread:
noah.sales: FYI AcmeBio wants a short POC (2 weeks) using a Dedicated endpoint. Their infra team says their egress IPs are ephemeral (autoscaling jumpboxes). They asked if we can front them with a stable egress or recommend alternatives + whether POC usage will count vs a future Reserved commitment.

tara.eng: We can provision a dedicated pool for the POC and attach static egress addresses (our side). Typical quick pattern: we create the pool, allocate 1-2 /32 public IPs, and hand those to the customer for allowlisting. That avoids them changing their outbound NAT.

diego.net: If they can NAT to a stable EIP on their side that's the cleanest approach (their firewall only needs the fixed IP). If they cannot, options:
- Proxy / NAT on our side (we expose static egress IPs)
- Hostname/SNI allowlist combined with short-lived bearer tokens (works but more brittle; SNI lacks client auth)
- mTLS for Private/VPC installs (requires cert exchange and is more setup-heavy)

rachael.solutions: On billing: sales can request a POC carve-out. We normally either credit the POC usage or mark it as excluded from the customer's Reserved capacity window if an addendum is signed. I'll draft language; finance needs the pool ID and dates.

maria.sec: Security quicknotes: TLS 1.3 enforced, standard cipher suites, request logging in Console, optional mTLS for Private deployments. For Dedicated pools (hosted), we can publish a small set of static egress IPs per pool. If they want client certs, that requires Private (or Private-like configuration) so we can validate client CA. Also share SOC2 docs via Secure Portal.

noah.sales: Can someone drop a minimal allowlist + verification curl that the customer infra team can paste into their ticket? They need something they can hand to ops ASAP.

tara.eng: Pasted below — replace IPs/hostnames with values we give once pool is ready. Also include an example for SNI-based test.

```
# Allowlist example (replace with assigned egress IPs)
198.51.100.42/32   # dedicated-egress-1
198.51.100.43/32   # dedicated-egress-2

# Simple curl smoke test against Dedicated API
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFLOW_POC_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://dedicated-eu.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"ping"}' | jq .

# SNI-only smoke test (if using hostname allowlist)
curl -v --resolve "dedicated-eu.redwood.ai:443:198.51.100.42" https://dedicated-eu.redwood.ai/healthz
```

noah.sales: Great — they also asked: if we provide our static egress, do we rotate it automatically? They worry about IP change mid-POC.

maria.sec: We keep pool egress stable for the lifetime of the pool unless an incident/maintenance requires change. Non-emergency IP rotations are scheduled with >=48h notice. Emergency rotations will be communicated ASAP.

diego.net: Operational note: if customer uses SNI/JWT allowlist flow, advise a token TTL of ~10-15 minutes for short-lived tokens and set up automated rotation. Also document the list of hostnames they should allow (e.g., dedicated-eu.redwood.ai). SNI-only is not equivalent to mTLS.

rachael.solutions: Action items: (1) Sales to confirm POC dates and infra contact; (2) Engineering to provision pool and share assigned egress IPs; (3) Legal/Finance to agree on POC credit or exclusion and sign addendum. I'll coordinate with finance.

deploy-bot: [infra] created dedicated-pool/poc-acmebio by @tara.eng — pool-id p-9f8e7d6c — egress: 198.51.100.42, 198.51.100.43

noah.sales: Thanks all. I'll send the snippet to AcmeBio infra and schedule a 20m handoff Thu 9am CET. If they can't provide a NATed EIP, we'll proceed with our static egress and the POC addendum. :rocket:
